inspiration: Pack calls for help: monster policy rows carry separate help request and help response fields (apps/server/internal/game/world/monster/data/tactics_controls.json line 1). Field names only; the code that reads them was not read. Recreate the idea: one monster that is attacked calls allies within a radius, and the allies choose to answer or not.

Hive caps tied to the player count: the hive table has a max live count, a hive order and a monsters-per-player column (v1188_hive_caps.tsv line 4). Recreate the idea: a zone spawn cap that grows with nearby players up to a limit, which fits the spawn caps in row 23.

Keep-distance summoner: summoner rows list summon sets, sight range and a target policy (v1188_summon_tactics.tsv lines 1 to 3). Recreate the idea: a caster that backs off to a set range and calls a small group, distinct from our own summon rules.

Stamina and variance on a monster: each policy row has a max stamina and a variance field (field names only; the code that uses them was not read), which suggests a fight limit that differs per spawn. Recreate the idea: a per-spawn variance on the leash or flee threshold.

Aggro and target-change fields: a monster has a fixed aggro type and a target-change rule, so it can keep or drop its target on a set condition. Recreate the idea: a simple target-change rule in the engine hate list (many-on-one logic).

Separate tables for separate versions: the monster data is split into a v1188 table, an isror table and a supplement (monster/data/). Keep versions apart and join them by a stable codename, not a numeric id (population_evidence line 3 says so).

briefs.label: Pack that calls for help
briefs.why: A single pull turns into a group fight, which gives many-on-one pressure without a boss.
briefs.keep: a help request from the attacked monster, a response that allies may decline, and a radius
briefs.change: ours calls only when hit by a ranged or heavy attack, and the called allies arrive with a short wind-up tell; recreate as a clearly distinct original, not a copy

briefs.label: Zone hive that scales with players
briefs.why: Spawn density rises with the crowd and stops at a cap, so a quiet zone stays quiet.
briefs.keep: a max-live cap, a per-player step and an order that decides which hive fills first
briefs.change: ours uses zone coverage and the row 23 grace timer instead of a per-player column; the look is a new original creature, not the donor's

briefs.label: Caster that keeps its distance
briefs.why: A summoner that backs off reads as a threat to chase, and its summons add a second target.
briefs.keep: a keep-distance rule and a small summon set per caster
briefs.change: ours summons at a fixed cadence with a visible cast bar, and the caster has its own silhouette and palette
